sources.provenance: needs-baseline.json; reconstructed from the UCS, not independent stakeholder evidence.
OAL-P1/UCS.md, corrected baseline 0.2.1; original behavioral baseline 0.2.0.

canonical_content.narrative_role: partial narrative projection, not a complete reproduction
canonical_content.consistency_rule: ucs.json is the complete canonical structured source. UCS.md is a partial narrative projection: identifiers it cites must exist in ucs.json, and reproduced statements must agree with it. Omission of fields and sets not covered by the projection is permitted; a mismatch in reproduced content is a divergence.

facts.statement: A team can record work in a project backlog (N-WB-001).
A manager can assign a work item to a person (N-WB-002).
A team can advance work through a three-state workflow (N-WB-003).
A team can discuss an item through comments (N-WB-004).
A team can read the board and the discussion (N-WB-005, N-WB-006).
Sprints, estimates, notifications, public deployment, and user administration are outside this baseline.

baseline_notes: Version 0.2.0 makes field limits, priority values, whitespace normalization, and ordering explicit from the implemented contract and the edition review. These details were not stated in the 0.1.0 text; they are recorded as 0.2.0 baseline decisions, not as historical requirements. The same 0.2.0 edition now makes the storage-failure outcome and the unbounded positive expected-version input explicit; its identifiers and version are unchanged.
scope: One local team, work items grouped by project, a three-state workflow, and discussion.

actors.name: Manager
actors.description: Creates, assigns, advances, comments, and reads.

fields: description: at most 2000, may be empty
relations: A work item owns zero or more comments.
invariants: Surrounding whitespace is trimmed before length checks.
Only the next workflow state is admissible.
A stale version cannot overwrite a newer one.
entities.validity_location: applied by the cases in src/work_board/usecases/operations.py using required_text in src/work_board/entities.py

relations: A comment belongs to one work item.
invariants: Comments do not change the item version.
Comments are ordered by timestamp then identifier.

rules.statement: Project is 1-40 characters, title 1-120, and description at most 2000 after trimming surrounding whitespace; a whitespace-only value counts as empty. Assignee is 1-80 characters and comment text 1-1000 characters after trimming.
Priority is low, normal, or high; normal is the default and any other value is invalid.

An expected version is a positive integer. Assignment and advance are atomic compare-and-set operations: a stale version is rejected without changing the item. This input domain has no storage-specific upper bound. An expected value that cannot match a stored version yields conflict for an existing item or not_found for an absent item.
The workflow is backlog to in_progress to done; only the next step is allowed, and a skipped step is rejected without changing the item.
A comment records the authenticated actor, trimmed text, and timestamp. Comments are append-only, ordered by timestamp then identifier, and do not change the item version or its records.
The board applies exact project and status filters and returns items ordered by project, title, and identifier, without mutation.

obligations.statement: Every case receives a resolved actor context and checks its role against the permitted set before domain effects. This example requires authenticated callers; the trusted entry point establishes the context but does not authorize the case.
verifiable_conditions: a known role outside the permitted set is refused
refusal leaves no domain or persistence effect

obligations.statement: Assignment and advance use an expected version and fail without overwriting a newer state.
verifiable_conditions: a stale version yields a conflict
the item is unchanged after the conflict

obligations.statement: Create, assign, advance, and comment are atomic with their records; comments do not alter the item version. Atomicity excludes partial records, but an unconfirmed commit does not establish that no complete write occurred.
obligations.origin_reference: UCS R-WB-05 and the store contract
verifiable_conditions: a confirmed rollback leaves the previous state intact; no partial record is reported as success
a comment insertion does not change the item version

obligations.statement: The form exposes length limits and the next workflow step so the interface agrees with the domain contract.
verifiable_conditions: the next state is presented consistently with R-WB-04

obligations.statement: The board returns all matching items for a small local team; pagination and throughput targets are not claimed.
Every case exposes storage unavailability as a stable failure with a declared write outcome and never presents an unconfirmed operation as successful.
obligations.origin_reference: Current 0.2.0 baseline review; not reconstructed stakeholder evidence.
verifiable_conditions: not_applied is used only when absence of a write is established
an unconfirmed commit or rollback is reported as unknown

use_cases.name: Create work item
use_cases.objective: Record work in a project backlog.
use_cases.trigger: An allowed actor submits a project and title.
preconditions: the actor is authenticated and permitted
results: A new item is in backlog with version 1 and no assignee.

criteria.text: A valid item stores project, title, description, priority, backlog status, and version 1.
A viewer or invalid required fields cannot create an item.
Storage failure yields unavailable without false success; confirmed absence of a write is distinguished from an unknown write outcome.

use_cases.name: Assign work item
use_cases.objective: Assign an existing item to a person.
use_cases.trigger: A manager names an assignee and the expected version.
preconditions: the actor is authenticated and permitted
results: The assignee is recorded and the version increases.
effects: the assignee and version of the item change
capabilities: update an existing item conditionally on its version

criteria.text: Only a manager can assign an existing item.
A stale version is rejected without overwriting a newer assignment.
Storage failure yields unavailable without false success; confirmed absence of a write is distinguished from an unknown write outcome.

use_cases.name: Advance work item
use_cases.objective: Advance work through the three-state workflow.
use_cases.trigger: An allowed actor requests the next state with the expected version.
preconditions: the actor is authenticated and permitted
results: The item advances backlog to in_progress to done, one step at a time.
effects: the status and version of the item change
capabilities: update the status conditionally on its version

criteria.text: A valid next step changes the state and increases the version.
A skipped step or stale version is rejected without changing the item.
Storage failure yields unavailable without false success; confirmed absence of a write is distinguished from an unknown write outcome.

use_cases.name: Add comment
use_cases.objective: Discuss an item without changing its version.
use_cases.trigger: An allowed actor submits comment text for an existing item.
preconditions: the actor is authenticated and permitted
results: A comment records author, text, and time without changing the item version.
capabilities: persist a comment for an existing item

criteria.text: A valid comment is retained with its actor and timestamp.
A viewer, empty text, or absent item cannot add a comment.
Storage failure yields unavailable without false success; confirmed absence of a write is distinguished from an unknown write outcome.

use_cases.name: View board
use_cases.objective: Read matching work items without mutation.
use_cases.trigger: An actor requests the board, optionally filtering project or state.
preconditions: the actor is authenticated and permitted
results: Matching work items are returned without mutation.
alternatives: an empty result is a successful response
capabilities: read work items with exact filters

criteria.text: An allowed actor can see all items or only a selected project or state.
An unknown state filter is rejected.
Storage failure yields unavailable without false success; confirmed absence of a write is distinguished from an unknown write outcome.

use_cases.name: View comments
use_cases.objective: Read an item's discussion without mutation.
use_cases.trigger: An actor requests discussion for an item.
preconditions: the actor is authenticated and permitted
results: Its comments are returned in time order without mutation.
alternatives: an item without comments returns an empty list
capabilities: read comments for an existing item

criteria.text: An allowed actor can read an item's comments, including an empty list.
An absent item is reported as absent.
Storage failure yields unavailable without false success; confirmed absence of a write is distinguished from an unknown write outcome.

actor_context.actor_meaning: The specified actor is a role performed by a person or system requesting a case.
actor_context.authentication: Required by this example for every case.
actor_context.representation: An explicitly supplied resolved role identifier (manager, contributor, viewer). The trusted entry point establishes the role; principal is the implementation parameter for this context.
actor_context.denial: Missing or unknown context and roles outside the case permitted set are refused before domain effects. This example does not admit anonymous requests.

unavailable.meaning: The storage operation could not confirm a successful result; no success is reported.

write_outcome.not_applied: The operation failed before a write, or its uncommitted changes were confirmed rolled back.
write_outcome.unknown: The write outcome could not be confirmed, including a failure during commit or rollback.

unavailable.recovery: When the outcome is unknown, inspect current state before deciding whether to retry; a failure response alone does not imply absence of effects.

stable_revision.change: O-WB-AVAIL origin classification corrected to domain; original origin_reference retained; no behavioral change.
